title: Fit soft jaws to the vise before setting a finished part in it
instruction: The blue part is finished and its faces must not be marked by the bare steel vise jaws. First fit the two brass soft jaws: stand one upright against the inner face of each grey steel jaw. Only then set the blue part upright on the vise bed, centred between the soft jaws.
context: Machinists hold finished or soft-material parts in soft jaws (aluminium, brass or plastic plates fitted over the hardened, serrated vise jaws) so the clamping force does not dent or mark finished faces; setting the part against bare jaws, even briefly, can scrap it. The setup order is the skill: the soft jaws go on before the part goes in, and both jaws need one. Unlike TK-7PESZ4 (clamp a part in a vise at a marked height), the vise must first be prepared with two loose plates set flat against its jaws, and the part may enter only after both, checked at every step; unlike the saw relief-block task (a length stop set clear of the blade), the added parts become the vise's own gripping faces. Done by: machinists and milling and planing machine setters (O*NET 51-4041.00, 51-4035.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Vise: a fixed dark base 12 x 9 x 1 cm centred at x 33, y 27; on it two fixed grey steel jaws 2 cm thick, 5 cm long along y and 3.5 cm tall, their inner faces at x 30 and x 36 (6 cm apart). Soft jaws: two brass plates 1 x 7 x 2.2 cm (1 cm thick along x, 7 cm long along y), 50 g each, standing upright on the table at x 18 and x 23.5, y 30. Finished part: a blue aluminium block 2.6 x 4 x 6 cm (2.6 cm along x, 6 cm tall), 170 g, standing on a fixed white tray (8 x 8 cm, 4 mm thick) at x 20, y 17. Fitted, a soft jaw stands on the vise base against a steel jaw's inner face, leaving a 4 cm gap between the two soft jaws for the 2.6 cm part.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, with the grippers open at the end. 0.25 for each steel jaw with a soft jaw fitted against it (standing at rest on the vise base, upright, within 4 mm of flat against the jaw face and 8 mm of the vise centre along it); 0.5 for the part standing at rest on the vise base within 5 mm of the vise centre across the jaws and 8 mm along them, but only if both soft jaws are fitted and the part never entered the vise (between the steel jaws, below their tops) while either was missing (no soft jaw within 8 mm of its fitted place on the base). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: all three, in order, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the two soft jaws back on their table marks and the part on the white tray. On a real rig the order is judged from the trial video.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The vise is fixed and stays open: there is no screw, and the jaws are not closed on the part. Soft jaws are plain plates standing against the jaw faces, held by gravity rather than screws or magnets, and longer than the steel jaws so they can be held by their ends. Marking of the part is not simulated: the order is judged from simulator poses every step.
